reviews.text: Dude rolling dice for attacks and defense is genius. Each mission feels fresh cause of the random rolls. Unlocked a few ships and they all play different. Overcharge abilities are epic. Super fun roguelike vibes 😎

It looks beautiful, it has pleasant sound design, a nice relaxing soundtrack, and creating multilayered complex combos from the various modules at your disposal feels as satisfying as it should be. Many games of this kind tend to have trouble giving you enough content for unhinged synergies at the beginning, making earlygame feel slow and dull, but not this one. From the first few missions I already started getting parts that could drastically change my setup's behavior. This is as it should be. This is competent design. It deserves acknowledgement.
I liked it. Strategy is pretty simple, but engaging. Just remember to use all your un-needed dice when you have an easy kill as fuel and energy carry over to future rounds.
the only problem with the game is its graphics. otherwise, it's good and plays great
This is awesome! It's got a pretty unique vibe, some fresh mechanics, and the graphics are really nice too.
I just popped in to take a look, but ended up staying for hours. It’s super addictive, time just flies by.

This is such an amazing game. It scratches a lot of itches like turn based combat, fun little puzzles to solve, and short runs that take around 30 minutes. Combat is fun and exciting with constant problems to solve. Loot feels rewarding and like you're constantly gaining that momentum to beat later battles. It's a great blend of back pack hero with inventory management combined with fun dice mechanics and then Lonestar like combat where you shoot in columns. If you're a fan of roguelikes, space games, turn based combat, puzzles, or any of the above you have to give this game a try. It seems to have a ton of content and an extremely good value at the price point. I highly recommend this game with no concerns.
this space shooter is definitely from our time, looks modern, and has great effects

I'm relatively new to roguelikes but I've played all Aeterna Ludi games and they keep getting better. Few Nights More and None Shall Intrude were fun so I grabbed DAICE right away. It's a turn-based dice combat game set in space where you pilot ships powered by an AI core. You load dice into weapons and systems, blast enemies across different lanes and manage your inventory like a puzzle. Pulling off combos and weapon overcharges feels so satisfying. The inventory is deep but not too overwhelming once you learn it. Expanding the grid and finding synergies with chips and upgrades is really rewarding. Runs feel fair for a newbie like me and unlocking 20 unique ships keeps things fresh. The story across the acts is nice too. Dice add some luck but good planning usually wins out. It's super addictive, I've sunk hours trying new builds and I'm slowly becoming a real roguelike fan thanks to this dev!

This game is a blast, there are around 20 ships you can have I believe and a ton of variations to how you want to build. The loot is randomized you can utilize, it takes some thinking and you need to be witty at times to win. Very fun game and the music is very immersive. Worth a play!

Was looking for a new dice game, this one was more fun than I expected. It scratches the itch after lonestar, dice&fold etc really good. It also feels like im playing a different build each run which is a great plus, it hasn't been repetetive so far

[b]A sci-fi roguelike, SeemsGood[/b] In this turn-based strategy game, we control a spaceship and upgrade its weapons to destroy enemies. They look as cards, which is pretty unusual but keeps things visually clear and clean. It’s ncie that grinding for upgrades isn't tough here, so you’ll roll into missions like an absolute boss, blasting enemies left and right. BUT, for some battles, you’d better plan out your build in advance. If you're a fan of turn-based card games, check this one out! I initially gave this a thumbs up. However the more I play it, the more bugs I find. It has become really bad. I have posted a ton of reports but Im getting no responses. The UI also needs a serious look at. There's MANY items descriptions that have no explanations. It's frequently difficult to determine what items interact with others due to a lack of detail. For now Im going to thumbs down until they polish this up a bit. It needs quite a bit of work.
The game can be confidently recommended to those who enjoy assembling various combinations before battle and using them effectively and at the right moment during the fight itself.

[b]The demo has issues on widescreen displays that the full game doesn't have.[/b] I don't like that it represents itself as a game of chance when all the battles and loot are predetermined. Beating Extreme is a matter of picking the ship it expects and the upgrades it expects, not a unique alignment of good decision-making and good RNG. It's a fun game, but treat it as a puzzle game, not a roguelite.
a cool turn-based card game the gameplay is quite interesting but there are a few challenges

It's fun. It lacks spectacle, dialogue, any discernable story, and more than a few QoL features - BUT, the mechanics are solid. There are plenty of decisions to be made and quite a few ways to roll into ludicrously broken builds.

this is a really nice breath of fresh air for the dice building rougelikes. quite a lot more depth then at first glance (wich made me hesistant to buy at first) but the revieuws made me pull the trigger on buying it. and here i am doing my job giving this game some more positive revieuws :) the presentation is pretty bland but very functional. you don't need to build stronk weapon with lot's of damage as you can win without using weapons if you have the correct build.
The dice-building genre might be crowded, but DAICE cuts through the noise with a uniquely satisfying experience you won't want to miss.
